Wobbuffet answers a big hit with Counter or Mirror Coat, or Encores

attempts.party: party_gym76.json (Incineroar / Urshifu-Single / Gengar / Hydreigon / Weavile / Zapdos)
attempts.why: The trap never closed. Turn 1 Fake Out flinched Wobbuffet and a single always-crit Wicked Blow took all 440 of its HP before Counter could resolve; a critical Focus Blast from Reuniclus took Incineroar from full the same turn. Turn 2 Wicked Blow removed Reuniclus as it Calm Minded, and Zapdos's Thunderbolt, redirected off the fainted target, took Swoobat (+2/+2 from one Simple Calm Mind) from full. Wicked Blow removed Specs Indeedee turn 3 while Munkidori's Toxic Chain badly poisoned Zapdos; turn 4 Wicked Blow removed Munkidori but its Sludge Bomb finished the poisoned Zapdos and Azelf's Dazzling Gleam put Urshifu on its sash. Ice Shard plus Sucker Punch ended Azelf on turn 5.

protect_summary: No opponent Protect in five turns. Reuniclus, Munkidori and Azelf all carry Protect and chose to attack or set up instead; each of those choices was defensible on the visible board and two of them cost me a Pokemon.
observations: Wicked Blow's always-crit is doing more than my paper figures throughout this block (440 to a 252 HP / 4 Def Wobbuffet from a 274-Attack Urshifu). Not a defect claim - I cannot read the ROM's crit multiplier from the driver - but the main agent may want to confirm the crit multiplier is 1.5 and not 2.0, because a 2.0 crit would explain every 'harder than it reads' Wicked Blow and Knock Off number in receipts 247-251.
level_change_rationale: Keep. Won on attempt 1 with two faints, both to the room's real special damage (a crit Focus Blast, Toxic Chain plus Sludge Bomb). The brief's keep case. I considered +1 on Wobbuffet because the centrepiece died to one hit, but that is a design question (a 58-base-Defense wall versus an always-crit Dark move) and not a level one; +1 would not have saved it.
concept_on_board: No, and that is the finding. The room's idea - 'you cannot switch and the thing preventing you cannot be safely attacked' - was on the board for exactly one action. Wobbuffet's whole design assumes the player attacks it once and eats Counter; a 4-Def-EV Wobbuffet against a 2x always-crit STAB move does not get its turn. Simple and Toxic Chain and Magic Guard all showed, but only as things I removed the same turn they appeared.
cooler: The concept is the strongest in the gym on paper and the weakest in play, for one reason: Wobbuffet is physically paper. Two notes, not implemented. (1) Wobbuffet's spread is 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpD Calm; against this cap window the physical Dark hit is the first thing any player brings, so a 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD Bold spread (Mirror Coat still covers special) or at least a split would let it live to Counter once. (2) The room's payoff bodies (Reuniclus, Swoobat) are in slots 2 and 3 and arrive while the player still has full offence; Wobbuffet leading alone with Azelf (Sash + Nasty Plot) would let Azelf punish the turn the player spends on the wall. Toxic Chain Munkidori was the best body here and the only one that took a Pokemon by design rather than by crit.
